newsitem.title: USA: Trading cards maker Pinnacle to launch IPO.
newsitem.headline: Trading cards maker Pinnacle to launch IPO.

text.p: Pinnacle Brands Inc., the hockey, baseball and football trading card company, hopes that investors will want to trade its own stock, when it launches this week a $60 million initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange.
Pinnacle sells sports trading cards under eight brand names including Score, Select, Pinnacle, Action Packed and Racer's Choice.
The company, which had a 37 percent market stake in those three sports last year, plans to offer four million shares on Thursday.
The shares are estimated to be priced between $14 and $16. The offering is tentatively scheduled to be priced Wednesday for trading on Thursday.

The IPO is expected to generate $55 million, and Pinnacle said it will use $22 million of the total to reduce its debt under a credit agreement and $33 million to repay money owed to its largest stockholder, Acadia Parners LP. After the offering, Acadia will own 65 percent of the company.

Pinnacle posted a 1995 loss of $2.4 million on revenues of $130.2 million. Its baseball and hockey card sales have not yet recovered from a slump suffered after the 1994 Major League Baseball strike and work stoppage at the National Hockey League.
